newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BOND, FX MOVE LARGELY TEMPORARY - CBANK SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BOND, FX MOVE LARGELY TEMPORARY - CBANK SOURCE.

text.p: Greece's central bank views recent turbulence in forex and bond markets as largely temporary and will stick to its anti-inflationary monetary and foreign exchange policy, a central bank official told Reuters.

"The monetary and foreign exchange policy of the central bank will remain anti-inflationary in character," the official said. "Our assessment is that recent developments in forex and bonds reflect temporary factors."
The drachma has exhibited weakness against the ecu in recent days, forcing the central bank to intervene and sell large amounts of ecus and marks at the fixing to support the currency.
The Bank of Greece sold 350 million ecus and 80 million marks for drachmas at the fixing on Tuesday but this did not stop the drachma from slipping to 311.90 versus the ecu from 311.370 on Monday.
Prices of fixed coupon bonds and zeros have also lost ground in recent days shedding 50 to 80 basis points.
"Recent bond sales could relate to ecu purchases for drachmas from abroad but it is not clear how strong the correlation between them is at this point," the official said.
Some foreign investors seem to be reassessing their positions in view of increased uncertainty in European forex markets due to the French election outcome, the official said.

Bankers have also pointed out that reduced interest rate differentials between Greece and some of its major EU partners have contributed to the weakening of the drachma and made local financial assets less attractive. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
